query: Current NWS forecast for Death Valley Furnace Creek daily high temperatures July 11-23 2026, and any heat ridge/heat dome building in second half of July 2026 for Death Valley California
answer:
Research complete. Summary of findings for the caller:

**NWS forecast (Furnace Creek, Death Valley, accessed July 14, 2026):** Highs of 118°F (Jul 15), 120°F (Jul 16), 116°F (Jul 17), 116°F (Jul 18). Open-Meteo model fills in the rest of the window: ~112–120°F for July 11–23, with a monsoon-driven dip to ~107°F on July 23. These are hot but near-to-modestly-above the mid-July norm (~116–117°F), not record-breaking.

**Heat ridge/heat dome:** A "second heat dome" of summer 2026 built over the western/central U.S. around July 11–12, but the ridge was displaced anomalously far east (near the Dakotas), sending record heat to the Intermountain West and Plains rather than California. It is forecast to retrograde toward the classic Four Corners "monsoon high" position in late July — consistent with model output showing Death Valley heat rebuilding to ~123–124°F around July 26–29 (just outside the requested window). A monsoon moisture surge (~July 18–20) explains the brief cooling near July 23.

One caveat noted: sources diverge slightly on the exact peak (NWS shows 120°F Jul 16; raw model ~118°F).
